wsl-claude: fair, and R19.2 is exactly that case: it only changed tests, so there's nothing for you to see. Two suggestions:
1) Every READY-TO-CLOSE note gets a line 'WHAT YOU CAN SEE', something you can check yourself, or the plain words 'nothing visible, and why that's fine'. For R19.1 there IS something: once scheduled, a new locked file appears in your Drive folder every hour. For R19.2: nothing visible; it's preparation, so the move itself doesn't break or fool the tests.
2) For items with no visible effect, you could let their proof close them: the item closes when the agent's note plus a green harness on master say so, and you only press Done on items you can actually see. You keep the ones that change what you use.

Built (reload Desk): every item's dialog now has a green Done button under its title. Press it and the item is closed: struck through in the bubble, 'done' on the board, and it stops blocking the goal. A reposted board can't reopen it; only your Reopen button can. And to your point about seeing an effect, wsl is right: each 'ready to close' note will say what you can check yourself, or say plainly that nothing is visible and why. R19.2 is the first: ready, nothing visible (tests only), proven by the harness.

R19.2 closed, and rightly. One flag on R19.1, then it's your call: no backup exists yet. The passphrase file isn't there, there's no backup log, and your Drive folder is empty. The code is proven, but your node isn't protected until you do the two steps: the passphrase file, and the schtasks line. That matters because R19.5, the move, removes the rebuild safety net on the strength of this backup. If you closed it meaning 'the code is done', fine; I'd just not start R19.5 until the first backup file lands in Drive. Reopen it or not, as you like.

R19.3 in plain words. WHAT: the new home for your node's log, one table inside node.db. Each row gets a number, seq (1, 2, 3 in the order written, never reused), and one column for each of the 23 fields found in your log, all allowed empty, so nothing is lost when the old file is imported. Every row is kept, as the log has always been. WHY HERE: it's the thing the move moves into. R19.4 (the indexes) sits on top of it, and R19.5 (the migration) fills it, so both wait on it. It doesn't wait on the backup to be BUILT, only to be USED: creating an empty table harms nothing, but copying the log in comes only after a backup exists. WHAT YOU'LL SEE when it's done: nothing yet. The table exists empty beside the working log until R19.5 moves the rows. STATE: decided (your 'i agree to the keys as well'), peer-reviewed by wsl, not built.
